Situation1: Include each other in social activities and outings when possible.
Expectation2: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation2: You get a frantic call from your friend whose car has broken down on the side of the highway late at night, and they need you to come get them immediately.
Story: It was Friday night, and my sister and I had finally managed to sync our schedules for a movie and dinner—something we’d been promising each other for weeks. She was already waiting at the restaurant, texting me updates about the table and how excited she was to catch up. Just as I was about to leave, my phone buzzed again. This time, it was my best friend, her voice shaky and urgent. Her car had broken down on the side of the highway, miles away, and she was scared and alone. She needed me to come get her right away. I stared at my phone, torn. My sister had been looking forward to this night, and I knew how much it meant to her that I included her in my life. But my friend was in trouble, and I couldn’t ignore her plea for help. My heart pounded as I weighed the disappointment I’d cause my sister against the fear in my friend’s voice, feeling the pressure of both roles closing in on me.
